record.original_question: For a simple connected unsigned graph Γ, determine the signature or signatures σ̄ that minimize spectral radius among all signatures on Γ, that is, satisfy ρ(Γ, σ̄) <= ρ(Γ, σ) for every signature σ of Γ.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.18 (Signature minimizing the spectral radius). Let Γ be a simple and connected unsigned graph. Determine the signature(s) σ¯ such that for any signature σ of Γ, we have ρ(Γ, σ¯) ≤ ρ(Γ, σ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair (Γ, σ) consisting of a simple connected unsigned graph Γ = (V, E) together with a signature σ : E → {+1, −1}. The adjacency matrix A(Γ, σ) is the symmetric |V| × |V| matrix whose (u, v)-entry equals σ(uv) if uv ∈ E and 0 otherwise. The spectral radius ρ(Γ, σ) is the largest absolute value among the eigenvalues of A(Γ, σ).

Two signatures σ and σ' on Γ are switching-equivalent if there exists a function θ : V → {+1, −1} such that σ'(uv) = θ(u) σ(uv) θ(v) for every edge uv; switching-equivalent signatures yield similar adjacency matrices and hence the same spectrum.

Problem. Let Γ be an arbitrary simple connected unsigned graph. Characterize, up to switching equivalence, the signature(s) σ̄ on Γ that minimize the spectral radius, i.e. that satisfy
   ρ(Γ, σ̄) ≤ ρ(Γ, σ)
for every signature σ of Γ. In particular, give a structural or combinatorial description of such minimizing signatures for general Γ.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of identifying signatures that minimize the spectral radius of a signed graph is listed as an open problem in the spectral theory of signed graphs and is connected to the construction of expander graphs. Subsequent literature (e.g., works on unbalanced signed graphs with extremal spectral radius and on signed graphs with bounded spectral radius) addresses special cases and related extremal questions, but a general characterization for arbitrary simple connected graphs has not been established.
